title: Invariant-Preserving Scoring in a Chronos-Interpreter Social-Interaction Engine: A Balanced Search & Indexing Perspective
topic: I Read X s Open-Source Algorithm: One Reply From a Mutual Is Worth 30 Likes
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a formally verified scoring engine for a social-interaction platform implemented in Chronos-Interpreter. The engine aggregates likes and replies, applying a 30-point bonus for replies from mutual friends. We model the engine as a deterministic state machine, prove that the total score equals the weighted sum of all relevant interactions, and establish that the algorithm runs in $O(\log N)$ time per interaction, where $N$ is the number of stored interactions. Static analysis of the abstract syntax tree confirms a concise implementation with 190 SLOC and four function blocks. The source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Chronos-Interpreter-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261104_080123_i_read_x_s_open-source_algorit}.
